utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom and those assisting us just outside the courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar, I think the first thing we have to do is to deal with the documents tendered during the testimony given by Witness DP16. Could you please guide us, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1808, under seal, pseudonym sheet; Exhibit D1809, map of Sarajevo marked by witness; D1810, map; Exhibit D1811, map sniping incident 20 marked by witness; Exhibit D334, photograph of various buildings; D339, photograph of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since I do not hear any objections, the documents are admitted into evidence. D1808, under seal. I told the parties that the Chamber would give them an opportunity to briefly discuss the matter of the -- the matter of the maps. Mr. Ierace, I think we put some questions to you and I take it that you will further inform the Chamber about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. President. I have some copies of some maps to hand up and to distribute.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Do the Defence have a copy of these maps already, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't think so. Mr. President, firstly in relation --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise. I didn't want to start by interrupting Mr. Ierace, but for the sake of courtesy, General Galic should also have a copy as well as the Defence. We only have one copy of this. Would my learned colleague, Mr. Ierace, be able to provide us with a second copy so that the General can follow the matter we are dealing with. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, firstly in relation to some specific questions posed last week, I understand that the map is -- was prepared in 1997, that is the map data which appears on it. That's only an approximate time, approximately 1997, it is the 7th edition of a U.S. -- United States military map. There was a question also asked in relation to buildings and I said that buildings -- last week I said that buildings are taken into account in terms of lines of sight. I have been informed that that applies only to very large buildings such as the medical facility which was relevant to incident, I think it was incident 14. That is in Kobilja Glava, in any event. That was a very large building. Mr. President, the bundle of maps which has been handed up I will now go through one at a time. If I could perhaps commence with map 2. I have numbered the maps in the top right-hand corner. This is similar to the map which I handed up last week, that map being map number one. You will note that added to it are two graphs. Those graphs I think should be self-explanatory. The blue line on the graph indicates the changes in elevation between on the left-hand side the suspected source of fire, and on the right-hand side the position of the alleged victim. So by consulting the height figures on the left axis, that is the vertical axis, and the distance figures on the horizontal axis, one then has an elevation, that is a side view of the height differences. One has to factor in the height above ground level at which the shot is fired, and the height of bullet entry of the victim. And in this particular case the height of fire of the trajectory, that is, how high above the ground the bullet was assumed to have commenced its path, is around 1 and a half metres, and the entry point is around a metre, something of that order. Turning to map number 3, one sees a further advantage of this software. Map 3 is a three-dimensional depiction of the topography for incidents 3 and 8. The positions of the victims are indicated by blue dots. The area of the suspected source of fire is indicated by a large red area. Last week the Defence pointed out that the map which was provided to them in our meeting earlier in the week showed a different depiction of what could be seen from the suspected source of fire along the line of fire from the map which is now number 1 and which I showed to the Trial Chamber last week. This map, number 3, explains why. If one assumes that the person who fired the round was positioned on the edge of that red area immediately above the escarpment, then clearly, as one can see from this picture, the person firing the round would have a much clearer view of the area immediately beneath him or her, whereas if the shooter was positioned towards the rear, that is more on the ridge and to the back of the area of the red circle, then from that position the person firing the round would lose sight of the ground immediately at the bottom of the escarpment. So this software is sufficiently sensitive to pick up those minor discrepancies. Turning to map number 4, one has the view that the shooter would have had of the areas where the two victims were at the time that were shot indicated by the blue dots. Map number 5 is also a topographical view, but this time the view indicated in the picture is above and behind the position of the alleged sniper. Map number 6 is a detail of the topography showing the red area and the two blue dots indicating the positions of the alleged victims. The software enables the degree of shade to be adjusted so that the features of the topography are more or if one wishes less apparent in the maps. Mr. President, given the problems that we have had, it seems to me that an appropriate usage of the software at this stage of the trial would be to provide, that is to tender, a second set of sniping and shelling scheduled incident maps without the front lines, the confrontation lines being depicted at all. The advantage of that second set would be to enable anyone to take precise measurements of distances between any two points which appeared on the maps. The relevance of the -- me pointing out the capability of the software, in particular its ability to project a three-dimensional image, is essentially to disclose the possession now by the OTP of that software. I don't propose to use that technology at this stage, but we reserve our right to seek to tender such maps, three-dimensional maps, in case in reply pursuant to the usual provisos to the Prosecution being able to call evidence in reply. Mr. President, if the Trial Chamber is minded to accept into evidence these maps, and one alternative is simply that the Prosecution tender them as soon as they are prepared. An alternative is at least to have them marked for identification at this stage and then formally tendered in case in reply. Thank you. Excuse me, Mr. President. Yes, that completes my submission on the maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Do I understand you well that you say I explained to the Chamber what are the capabilities of this software, but that at this very moment the Prosecution would just provide maps without confrontation lines similar as the maps we used earlier, but then not with the difference in longitudinal and what's the other -- so that we have -- latitudinal. So that there is no difference in longitudinal and latitudinal measurement, that's so that we are better able to use these maps to measure distances because there is no distorted view any more on the ground covered by the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Precisely, Mr. President. But if the Trial Chamber wished the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- to tender further material or further maps with Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the topography, then of course we would be open to doing that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a clear description of this software available? So if it would ever come at a later stage to tendering the -- these maps if the Prosecution would like to do so, that's at least the Defence and perhaps also the Chamber, apart from perhaps hearing testimony on how it works might have also a description of the software and so that we can see how it works and what kind of instructions are given to the computers in order to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I anticipate that we will be in a position to call evidence of that nature and evidence as to the application of the information which pertains to the trial to the software in order to produce the maps. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the Chamber would invite you to respond, but I think at this very moment what is at stake is, first of all, an explanation of software which is not tendered. So whether it is true or not, and whether the software is really capable of doing it, I think we will discuss that when maps are produced by the special features of the software are used, and we limit now ourself to the production of the single maps could be also a software problem. But I would not, for example, at this moment discuss anything about the height of where the person is who might have fired. Because at this moment the Prosecution is not intending to tender that. So I would limit the discussion to what the Prosecution wants to put on the table at this very moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you very much. First of all, I have been perturbed by the clarity. Because of the Prosecution statement I have managed to turn my computer off, but with regard to the essential matters, Mr. President, I am surprised, I am very surprised. I don't know if anyone has been able to understand anything of this explanation, but what the Defence wants to say is that this software has been on the market since 1997. So before Mr. Galic was arrested. In accordance with article 90(H) the Prosecution should have provided this information which it didn't do. What I want to say is that the Prosecution should have disclosed this information to us, if they had wanted to do so. And finally, it was impossible for us to cross-examine on the basis of these documents because they weren't provided to us at the time. Now that the Defence seems to have proved certain points, the Prosecution has remembered that this fantastic software exists and intends to use it to its own benefit. Our position, the Defence's position is very clear. This does not seem acceptable to us. The Prosecution should have done this before so that we could have taken advantage of this when the Prosecution's case was being presented and not now. All the more so, in the -- many of our witnesses have already been heard and we will not be able to provide them with these documents, if they are acceptable. And the Defence doesn't think that they will be. Thank you. In addition, Mr. President, one of the Judges from your Chamber asked for more details. We could provide them now, the map C2 comes from the geographical military institute in Belgrade. It is 1982 edition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it is the staff map. It is the staff map for the English booth. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for your information, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. One final question: If the Defence would ever -- would like to use the facilities of the software, would it be made available in one way or another? I can imagine that there are -- there might be problems as to the license agreements, but perhaps a solution could be found for that in one way or the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would the facilities, apart from this problem, be available for the Defence if they would have certain wishes?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. There is a license involved, but I am sure that we can work within the legal requirements of the license to produce maps required by the Defence with the software.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know how many computer technologists the Prosecution has, but we don't have any. Unfortunately we are only attorneys and I've -- I don't have much competence in this area. I can't work as a technician with this software, which is beyond me, I have to admit it. Even though I am not familiar with this software yet. We will never be able to do this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Of course the same is true for the Chamber, I think, but I do understand that the Defence feels handicapped by not having the same expertise at hand in this respect. Then, Ms. Pilipovic, I see that you are on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, Your Honour, with your permission. I would just like to ask a question to clarify the matter. I'd like to know whether we will be working on the 11th of December because Defence counsel has to organise itself for the sake of the witness. We would also like to have the Trial Chamber with regard to our submission for a change in the list. The submission was filed on the 29th of November. I am only putting these two questions to you now, but we could discuss this at a later stage. I would just like to know what the schedule is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I understand is that we will not be able to sit on the 11th. So but I'll give you final confirmation of that. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, does that mean that we are only sitting Monday and Tuesday next week at this stage

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would mean if Wednesday is the 11th and I think it is, then it would mean that we would only be sitting on Monday and Tuesday. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Not on Friday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, not on Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, a couple of matters, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps I first -- you asked for a change, Ms. Pilipovic in a request of the 29th of November. That was -- could you be a bit more detailed as you said a change you requested on the 29th of November, a change in the calling order of witnesses or...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your order, the Trial Chamber's decision to authorise us to change two witnesses on the list that we submitted to the Trial Chamber. Instead of those two witnesses who are on the list, we would like your permission to have other witnesses in their place. They would be scheduled for the same time and it would have to do with the same circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Has the Prosecution is aware of what change you propose, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Perhaps my colleague hasn't had the opportunity of having a look at the submission. That's why I said that we could talk about this, we could discuss this submission later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If the Prosecution would have an opinion on the request, please inform the Chamber. If you would prefer to respond later today, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am happy to do it now, Mr. President. But the English transcript indicates that my learned colleague referred to two witnesses. The submission we have received dated the 29th of November refers to the addition of four witnesses. So perhaps we could just clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see on the 29th the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And the deletion of none.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, did you give -- you gave a list of four Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. witnesses on the -- in the -- and on the 28th of October you gave names of prospective Defence witnesses. Could you please explain. You said two witnesses. That's not quite clear to me, Ms. Pilipovic. But I might not have prepared myself properly for this issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the submission in which we requested that two witnesses be heard and now four in this submission is within the time frame that we have. But all four witnesses said that they wanted to come to testify and Defence counsel would like all four witnesses to be heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So two witnesses are added to your list?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And since your list took all the time granted to you, is there any other witnesses that will not appear? Because you have to stay within your time limits. So is there any other witnesses that will then not be called? I know that some were not called and perhaps we should make an inventory one of these days to see --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... time. Is there as such, I am not talking about the total time involved, but is there as such any objection against having two names added to the witness list, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. There is no explanation in the motion as to why the Defence should be permitted to add witnesses to their witness list at this stage. When a similar situation arose in the Prosecution case, we had to demonstrate why we had not included those witnesses in the initial list. That's the first objection. The second objection is that the statement of facts to which the four witnesses will testify which is contained in paragraph 3 of the motion is inadequate. It is what could be described as a broad brush reference to be applied apparently to the whole four of them and gives no clear insight into what it is that these witnesses are expected to say. That is relevant to the issue of whether leave should be granted to the Defence to call the witnesses. It is not at all clear, for instance, whether their evidence will be repetitive of the evidence expected of other witnesses. Thank you. Or I might add, Mr. President, of each other, since it applies to the whole four of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, first of all, perhaps the Prosecution has only partially read this document that has been submitted in English. At the end of point 3 we indicated clearly that the other more enlarged information will be given to the Prosecution as soon as possible. That is one point. The second point is that what has been described here is largely sufficient. It is certainly very clear so that everyone can understand what this is about. It is about the relationship between the opposing parties and the UNPROFOR as well as about the problem of civilians who were in the middle -- who were in the middle of all this, who are the most important. Rather than to complicate matters I believe that this is sufficiently clear, but otherwise other points they will be brought to the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you say broader summaries will submit after it established who of the above mentioned witnesses are available to testify. I have not clearly in my mind how broad these summaries are at this very moment. Of course, apart from what I read in paragraph 3, there are other summaries provided apart from what we read in paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, more substantive information has not been submitted. I just want to clarify that these four new witnesses whose names we put in this submission, they are able to come before this Chamber as of the 8th of January. One of the reasons why we have asked for the change in the calling order of witnesses and for the new four witnesses, the reason is that two witnesses from this battalion that we had put on the list are unable to come on the 8th of January. And speaking to other witnesses, these four witnesses said that they would be able to come to the Tribunal and be heard on the 8th of January. That's the reason why in this submission we first asked for permission to put them on the list, and then if that is confirmed, we can give much more substantive information about what they are going to be testifying about and what their reasons so they would come to the Tribunal on the 8th of January. We have brought up the problem about the impossibility of the Defence to bring witnesses on the 8th of January because it is a holiday, but these witnesses have confirmed that they are able to attend on the 8th of January. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I first try to identify what the problems are we are facing at this very moment. The first issue is that two witnesses who cannot come to testify be replaced by similar witnesses who could testify, then, I take it on the same subjects, because they were in a similar position. That's the first issue. So witnesses being replaced by other witnesses because of the unavailability. The second issue is the addition of two witnesses to the list. That's a different matter. The mere fact that additional witnesses are available on the 8th of January is as such not a sufficient ground to add them to the list of witnesses. When the Prosecution wanted to add witnesses to their lists, then we asked for specific reasons why it was necessary to hear additional witnesses, why they were not on the list before. And since you now put four witnesses on the list, I think the Chamber, but I will give you a final answer to that, but the Chamber might ask you for additional information. And since I do understand until now that the summary of what they will testify about gives approximately a similar subject matter to testify upon, the question put by Mr. Ierace whether this would result in repetitive evidence should be answered as well by the Chamber. So after the break I will tell you in what detail the Chamber or at least today or tomorrow morning whether and in what detail the Chamber wants to receive additional information. And please keep in mind that these are two different things, replacing one witness by another or to add witnesses on the list. Then, is there any other issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Firstly, now that I better understand the application, I have no objection to two of the witnesses being swapped. I maintain my objection to an additional two witnesses being called. In other words, two of that list of four is not objected to by the Prosecution, but not four witnesses to be called. Mr. President, the Prosecution is unclear as to which witnesses the Defence proposes to call this week. We have not received the running list that we expected. I understand that DP51 is to be recalled tomorrow. I am not sure who is to be called today or who is to be called after today's witness and tomorrow's witness. It would be of assistance if we could have that clarified. We have some timetable difficulties on the Prosecution side. And secondly, whichever witness it is today, I would be grateful if the Trial Chamber could indicate whether its intention is to suspend that witness's evidence tomorrow morning to enable DP51 to be recalled. The reason I would be grateful to know that is that it impacts on which counsel will take today's witness because of some problems later in the week with attendance. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic, is the Chamber well informed that the Defence intends to called today Witness DP17?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who is then -- who do you intend to call today so -- that is what my information was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness is DP17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I asked, but there must be a translation problem then. If you would look at the English transcript, you will see that the Chamber expected Witness DP17 to be called. Did I say -- yes, I said DP17. So it is DP17. Ms. Pilipovic, the recall of DP51, Witness DP51 tomorrow, could you please tell us whether the Defence Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. would prefer to have the testimony of Witness DP17 suspended tomorrow in order to hear -- to examine Witness DP51, or would you rather wait until we have finished with Witness DP17 and -- I see you are nodding for the transcript. I do understand that you would prefer to finish with DP17 and then that DP51 would be recalled.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Witness DP17 has been here for 8 days now, I think. He was supposed to start last week, but because of the schedule, the way it was, he didn't make it. So that's why the Defence would like to have DP17 finished first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would there be any objection as far as the Prosecution is concerned so that the Chamber can consider what -- whether the Defence is allowed to first finish with Witness DP17?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in fact I'd prefer that we finish DP17 before we go to DP51. I am still unclear as to who comes after DP51.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps you could receive this information during the break from Ms. Pilipovic, and then the Chamber, of course, would also be very glad to have this information. So the parties do agree that we should finish Witness DP17. One of the other things, Ms. Pilipovic, and perhaps I might ask your attention for that, if you say that you could give in further detail the summary of the four witnesses to be called that are on the request of the 29th of November, it gives the impression, but please correct me if I am wrong, that as a matter of fact the Defence has not thoroughly investigated what to expect from certain witnesses before they are called, before they are invited to come to The Hague. And that of course is of some concern because a decision on whether it's useful for the Defence case to call a certain witness you would preferably be done before the witness comes to The Hague at large expenses for the Tribunal. Mr. Piletta-Zanin --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just to respond. What we know is that the truth comes very often from the shock -- from the clash of new facts. And now we are at this stage that the team as we work, this is how this is proceeding, and that's the reason why there is this extra thing that we didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This "extra thing" what are you referring to? I am not quite clear that I do understand you. Perhaps I should change to the French channel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. I was talking about the clash of ideas or the shock of ideas, and we were not speaking about extraordinary things, supplementary things, we were talking about a second level of investigation, and it is starting from that level, that in general then we get more information that we can communicate in detail to the opposing side. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the question of course is how much information is there before the witness comes to The Hague and has further conversations with counsel or the team. That's, actually, what I was asking the Defence. Is the Defence ready to call Witness DP17?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Usher, could you bring Witness DP17 into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. DP17, because that's how we will call you since protective measures have been granted in respect of you. Mr. DP17, we will not use your name in this courtroom, and your face is distorted so that it cannot be seen by the outside world. Before giving testimony in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that declaration. And the text is just handed out to you by Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution -- for the Defence. Ms. Pilipovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. DP17, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Before I start asking you questions, I am going to show you a document that I would like you to have a look at and to confirm whether the information which is contained on the sheet of paper is correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Yes, the information is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. DP17.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that this would be a good moment to go into private session so that we can get some more detailed information about Mr. DP17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will turn into private session, that means that the outside world will not hear what you are telling us from now on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are not yet. Now we are. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, you told us on the 27th of May you were injured. And can you tell us a little -- with a little more detail, which area was that which you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Well, I started to say and then of course there was this thing. What proceeded the departure, you know that there were Serb students who were killed in this part of Grbavica. This was a Serb part of Sarajevo, and there was a --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, could you please just answer, in which area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: In Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP17 --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: I am sorry. Just if I can just explain how come I find myself in Dobrinja because --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We will ask you, Mr. DP17, if that is needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, may I ask you two things: The first is to wait until this text on your screen does not move any more so that means usually that the interpreters have translated the question. And if you would then answer the question. And the second thing I would like to ask you is to listen very carefully to the question. Because I am aware that you could tell us about your -- what you know for hours and hours, but the Defence is under certain time limits. So they will ask you especially what they would like to hear from you. And I am sorry for you, but you have to stick to the questions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, when you told us that you were wounded in Dobrinja, can you tell us whether at that time you were organised in a sense that you had weapons, and whether that was some kind of organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: At that time, when I was wounded we can already speak about organisation. But what is important is the direct link to this which is that following the killing of the wedding party guest in Bascarsija and the Serbo flag was certain fire, of course all civilians of Serb nationalities started to fear and be anxious about themselves and about their families.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, can you tell us, how were you organised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Well, to start with this was a spontaneous organisation. Because I knew that that part of the settlement, Sucuri Prapare and I moved my wife and children about 3, 4, 5 kilometres, deep into the area, also into the Serbian locality, and I saw passing by that time because my relative had a weekend cottage at that time -- and yes, I am just going to answer now. There was a return and there was a linking up with these people who were already there in Dobrinja, that would be my answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please be a little briefer in your responses. When you say that you organised yourselves, then you joined up. Those people who were organised in that part of Dobrinja, were you armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: When I arrived there, I wasn't armed but since in the nearby barracks there were weapons intended for the defence plan of the former SFRJ, these were weapons for the Territorial Defence, I was given a rifle, that is to say a Kalashnikov, from these weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP17, can you tell us what your military specialty is. Did you serve in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Yes, I did as a driver.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In September 1992 you said that -- you said where you joined up, you returned there. Can you tell us when the unit that you joined was formed? Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Do you mean the return after the hospital and then --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we are talking about September 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Yes, towards the end of May 1992 when the JNA units left, first of all, there was a spontaneous organisation and then companies, battalions were formed and the Ilidza Brigade, as well, and I returned that unit. I say that conditionally because I went there from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that you returned to the Ilidza Brigade, you told us how the Ilidza Brigade was established. Can you tell us where you were deployed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Well, since I was still not totally cured, I was deployed in the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. rear in the transport platoon. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, in September 1992 when you joined the Ilidza Brigade, can you tell us what the military situation in that Sarajevo municipality was like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: There were attacks on a daily basis launched by the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, do you personally know when the first attack took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Well, yes because on the 21st of April, in the evening, the line near Prapare Sucuri was attacked. There was intense shooting from the afternoon from 1800 hours up until perhaps 2100 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, I am asking you about --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: There was a frontal attack in Ilidza, but since we were also part of Ilidza, but to the eastern part of the municipality, my first -- this would be my first part of the answer. So it would be interesting to say that that attack that took place on the 22nd of April, the people from the delegation who went to negotiate with the Muslims in Hrasnica and in Sokolovica they said that they shouldn't attack, that it was pointless to die for no reason that it was necessary to stop the war. Bosiljcic Ljubo an attorney from Ilidza was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, I have to interrupt. You have to listen carefully to the questions and answer to the questions put by Ms. Pilipovic because there might be that things that you are telling us we might have heard already from other witnesses and Ms. Pilipovic wants to avoid that we hear things five, six, or seven times. There maybe other reasons why it is important for the Defence to put specific questions to you and very often you tell us what you know, but not always in relation to the question. For example, when Ms. Pilipovic asked you when your unit was formed, you gave a long answer, but I still do not know when your unit was formed. You don't have to answer it now. But if the Defence wants to get further information of you why things were important or who was involved or -- they will ask you. So please listen carefully to the questions and answer to those questions. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, since the witness mentioned names of some people, perhaps it would be good for the sake of the transcript to repeat those names and then I will move on to the specific questions. So I see that these names haven't been entered into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The people who were involved in the negotiations to avoid attacks, you mentioned the people who were part of the delegation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Do I have to repeat that? Should I repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, slowly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Ljubo Bosiljcic, an attorney; Milenko Jaslar, a bank official; and Popovic, I can't remember his first name.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can see that the names are still not in the transcript, but I will write it down and then provide the names during the break so as not to waste time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17 -- Mr. DP17, you told us that in September you joined the Ilidza Brigade. Can you tell us when that brigade was formed? Did you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Well, it was formed, as I said, towards the end of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When in September you joined the Ilidza Brigade, can you tell us who formed that brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Well, the men were mostly territorial men, reserve officials, out of the active duty officials, I can only remember Pero Despotovic, the commander of that brigade, who was there for a few days and then was assigned some other duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP17, you told us that you were deployed in September 1992, you were assigned to the brigade. Can you tell us whether throughout the relevant time period from September 1992 up until August 1994, was that your military assignment throughout that period or were there certain changes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: I wasn't there all the times. There were certain changes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what changed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: I think it was in November or December 1992 I was transferred as a deputy for morale and religious affairs in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP17, can you tell us whether you were at that post as the assistant for morale and religious issues throughout that period, were you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: No. Towards the end of May or June, I was transferred as chief of security in the brigade. I was assigned those duties and then again in September 1993, I think in September 1994 I was assigned as chief of the brigade staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP17, can you tell us you said sometime in June you were appointed as chief, chief of security. Can you tell us what duties you had to perform as the chief of security?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Well, these duties mainly involved security in the zone of this brigade that I have mentioned, that we are talking about. For example, general security, the deserters who would turn to us, their comments, their observations. If necessary I could clarify this, I could tell you what we paid special attention to.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, we will return to that matter. You said that you were responsible for your brigade's zone of responsibility. Can you tell us what territory that zone of responsibility covered, what was the front line? What was the length of the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: The length of the front line was about 25 kilometres. The front line extended from the Miljacka River through the urban part of Ilidza over the Zel Ljeznica River and continued towards Igman where we joined up with the Igman Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, you have told us what the brigade's positions were, could you now use a map that the Defence will provide you with in order to mark the positions of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Yes, I think I could do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, Defence would like to show the map -- show a map to the witness. It is 3742.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, could you please take a black felt tip that you will be given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, may I ask you not to mark anything until specifically requested to do so by Ms. Pilipovic. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, using this map, could you mark the positions of your brigade on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: The positions extended from the Miljacka River through the Komerc warehouse, below the Komerc warehouse, below the railway track in this part --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If you would just move your hand so that we can see what you are marking.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, can you tell us what part of town this is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: This is the Aerodromsko neighbourhood, I can't see this -- this is the Aerodromsko neighbourhood across the road from the airport. This is the western part of Dobrinja and in the direction of Nedzarici. We have this part here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, may I just intervene.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This map is presumably also of 1982 or this might even be the map, I am not quite sure about that, that you used. But as far as I understand maps until now, this map does not really reflect the situation the witness is testifying about. And he might be confused Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. since specifically the Dobrinja area does not appear on this map in such a way that it would be comparable to the situation, at least as far as the Chamber, until now, understands the situation to be in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I can see that on the map, but the Defence also has a plan of the town of Sarajevo. Perhaps this map would be more useful for the witness. But I don't know whether he could use this map to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can draw the line with precision, but this map is too -- the layout is not very visible and letters are very small. So it is a little more difficult for me to find my bearings, but it shouldn't be a problem for me to draw the lines as they were at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, can you tell us what that area is, the one you are marking now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: This is the area around Nedzarici towards Stupsko Brdo, the Stupsko hill. I am looking for this crossroads in the direction of Kasindolska Street and the Dobrinja River. That's where the Dobrinja River is. I have finally found it. That is how the line went.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, when you arrived in September 1992, was the line as such throughout the period of the conflict? What period of time does this line concern, the line that you have just drawn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Well, this line was such throughout -- almost throughout the entire period of the conflict. When I arrived in Ilidza, there were very few changes. When I returned from the hospital to the line there were very few changes on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In which area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Well, in the entire Serbian Municipality of Ilidza, there were very minor changes, insignificant changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, in light of the current map the witness is using, the Prosecution can certainly offer a clean copy of a much more detailed map if that would be of assistance. That is the only reason why I rise to my feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the Prosecution is offering you -- it might be confusing what we are doing now because we all have -- after few months we have the --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a map which we have been using with all the witnesses and the Prosecution also provided us with this map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do I have to carry on drawing the line?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, thank you, but please wait a minute.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps this would be a good time to have a break and we could then be provided would a map and during the break the witness could mark the positions on that map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we usually have a break at -- after one hour and a half, but it might be a good idea to ask the witness to mark the lines on a map during the break, on a map which reflects the situation as it did exist in 1992. We might get confused. But if you have any other questions for a couple of minutes, but we could have a break now and then for half an hour, and then -- Mr. DP17, you will be provided with another map that gives better picture of the situation as it existed in the beginning of the conflict. This Chamber, of course, has a different picture of Dobrinja compared to what it sees on this map, and therefore, it is also for our convenience that you will be asked to mark this lines you know about on a different map. Would you please be so kind to do that during the break so that we can see the result afterwards. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission I can give the witness part of the map of the town of Sarajevo which we have used in the course of examining by Prosecution witnesses and Defence witnesses. Perhaps we would use this map. It is in colour and it might assist all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That is fine, Mr. President. We just thought that this current map was not too helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until 10 minutes past 4 and we have the usual procedure as far as the presence of the parties is concerned during the marking of the witness, that is. I think it is done in the courtroom and both parties can be present and I don't know whether it assists to do it on the ELMO so that you could even follow what the witness is marking. I don't know whether this functions. So it is not. So we will wait for the result. We will adjourn until 10 minutes past 4.00

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we adjourned, we dealt with some issues. The Chamber has considered whether witnesses can added to the list, so that make them from 2 to 4, and the Chamber has decided that on the basis of the information provided, these witnesses, two of them can replace witnesses that earlier were on the list, but on the basis of this information the Chamber does not grant permission to add witnesses to the list. And in order to -- if the Defence would provide further information, then I think the proper way of doing it is first to give summaries of what we can expect from these witnesses, even if they are not in The Hague at this very moment, because that should be done before they come to The Hague. So the Chamber grants permission to replace two of the witnesses by two witnesses mentioned in the request of the 29th of November, and does not grant permission to add two other witnesses to the list. Then, of course, it is of importance for it Prosecution and for the Chamber to know which of the four -- which two of these four witnesses will replace the witnesses earlier listed. Since the parties agree that it would be better to first conclude with the testimony of Witness DP17, the Chamber agrees with that so that we do not suspend his testimony tomorrow, but first finish with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When I said that before on the basis of this information the Chamber did not grant permission to add these two witnesses to the list, that includes that if there would be good reasons, then, of course, we will consider that. But as it stands now, permission is not granted. And apart from that, of course, the time limits stay the same and we will deal with that relatively soon in more detail. Then, I take it that the witness has marked the map during the break. Perhaps we could, when the witness returns, have that on the ELMO so that we can see what he marked. And would there be copies of the map the witness used for the Chamber available as well so that we can reproduce his markings? I then think that we could ask the witness to come to the courtroom again. Could you please escort him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated. Please be seated, Mr. DP17.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the marked map be put on the ELMO so that the Chamber can see what markings have been made by Mr. DP17 during the break. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime, we believe that we have given one extra map. Could we have it back because we might need it? Oh, we haven't? Okay, very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Could we zoom out so that we can see -- yes. If we would just leave it there for a while so that the Chamber can... Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, so on this map you have marked in the positions of your brigade. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, before the break you told us that these positions didn't change significantly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say this, do you mean that these were the positions from 1992, that is when you came, and from 1993 and 1994 too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Well, there is a change here, that is, in order to answer this question, I have to say, first, the positions of the brigade and the Serb municipality of Ilidza, if you allow me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, could you please first show us on the map in your opinion where was this change in the positions, if there was a change? Could you use a pointer to show that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: It changed only inasmuch that in the part --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, could you turn towards the map and point with a pointer to your right, if you can point on the map this area. On your right -- on your right is the map and use the pointer to show this area. Can you move the hand. Now, can you use the pointer to show the area which changed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Only in this part, in this part of Otes here. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, when you say "in this part of Otes here" can you tell us when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: That was in early December in Otes in relation to the Patum locality, which there were Serbs who lived there. There were buildings that were dominant there. And from those buildings many civilians, women, children, elderly people were killed. So in one of the defence attacks, this part was liberated, this part that I am pointing to here. And this is probably the most important change as far as I can recall of the changes when we look at the whole map when I came to Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP, can you tell us, what was the name of that area, that area of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: That part was called Otes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP17, you marked this line for us. Is this a line which encompasses the entire area of the brigade, its entire line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: On this map, and I will again use the pointer to show this, it is not possible to see in front of the play park, there was a line that went between the great alley, Sokolovici, the colony. So this is the line between us, the colony Slavogonja [phoen] and towards Mount Igman so you cannot see that on this map. This is going south-west as we look on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you have explained that this south-westerly direction went to the foot of Mount Igman, is that how I should understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, can you tell us, considering that you have told us that the length, what was the front line. Can you repeat what the length was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: 25 kilometres, that was the length of the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us in terms of depth, how deep was the area of responsibility of the brigade in this part that you have drawn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: The area of responsibility of the brigade in terms of depth was 100 to 200 and depending on the layout of the terrain, sometimes even up to 2 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, when you asked the witness to point at the area where the front line had changed, do you intend to ask him to mark that as well? Because otherwise I would say that the witness pointed, and I will say it for the transcript, pointed at an area north from where it reads "Ilidza" and even north from a yellow road just above the word "Ilidza" approximately where what seems to be a railway line runs indicated on the map, Mostar Sarajevo. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. DP17, when you've told us about the depth of the area of responsibility of your brigade, can you tell us where were the command posts? And I am speaking about logistics and other units.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: The command post was slightly more forward than the front line, perhaps some 100 metres or somewhere a little further, while the logistics could be deep within the area, a couple of kilometres. But that was approximately the distance as far as the front line positions are concerned for the command post and for the logistics. The command of the brigade itself was about 300 metres from the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, can you tell us in certain areas I understood that the command posts were in the vicinity of the front line. Can you tell us what were the reasons for this disposition of the posts near the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: One of the main reasons, and on the map you can see that, that we were in fact surrounded and there was not much manoeuvreing space along the line. And in order not to endanger in this sense, considering that this whole area was under the dominant points where the Muslim forces were positioned starting from Igman, Mojmilo, Brijesce Brdo and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, so that we can all understand what you are talking about, can you tell us what were the dominant points? We understand that you can't see Igman, Mount Igman on this map, but --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: The dominant points were the entire area of Alipasino Polje that I am just pointing to, this here. There were buildings, 15 to 16 storeys high, then Vojnicko Polje about 10 storeys -- buildings of about 10 floors. Then the retirement old people's home, the Oslobodjenje building, the Mojmilo hill, Santica Hill from which we were targeted with cannons, with field guns. On the other side, what was also dominant, there was Vitkovac - let me just take my glasses - here is Vitkovac, Brijesko Brdo, Sokolje, so all of these elevation points including Mount Igman were all dominant, just like these buildings that I have named, they were all dominant in relation to our positions, because our positions were literally in the valley in a flat area. So all of the Ilidza Serb municipality is on a flat land, on a flat piece of land.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, on the map --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the transcript, do we need to describe these locations that Mr. DP17 described as being dominant elevation points --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, one could even ask oneself as to what extent this testimony is repetitive. I would say most of the positions the witness mentioned have been mentioned before. And as you know, the Chamber would very much like to parties to agree on where approximately what positions were and I do not see much contradiction in the testimony, perhaps, apart from some details, and sometimes in relation of time, but most of the elevated positions there seems to be not major disagreement between what the Prosecution witnesses have told us and what the Defence witnesses are telling us. Of course, they select other elevated points because they usually point to what elevated points were held by the other party. But apart from that, one could wonder what is the use of going through it all again. But I have got one question. The old people's home is now -- is on territory held by the other party. Could you please tell us what old people's home you have in mind when you said that it was a -- at a point or a building dominating. Could you indicate on the map where this old people's home is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is on the Muslim side next to the Oslobodjenje building which had about 20 storeys. And this retirement home or old people's home had 8 to 10 storeys. But that's what it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness pointed at where it reads "Dom Penzionera" which is on the --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, bearing in mind that Witness DP17 is the first Defence witnesses who specifically, according to his recollection, put in the lines of the brigade, this is the first Defence witness who has spoken about the lines of the brigade. It is not contested that we have heard Defence witnesses who have spoken about the positions of the battalions within this brigade, but we've only been able to hear witnesses who were speaking about areas of Nedzarici and Dobrinja. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. And now on the map we have the positions of the brigade. So we have somewhat a wider area of responsibility in relation to what the witnesses have testified so far.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, can you tell us in your brigade how many soldiers were on the front line per one kilometre in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Well, precisely it is hard to give an answer, but up to 70 soldiers could have been per 1 kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, can you tell us what was the deployment of soldiers on the first front line in your brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Most of the war events and battles, the so-called full combat readiness, which means that it is easy to establish the number of kilometres along the line as I have already told you about. The number of people in the brigade went from 2.000 to 2.500 people and to keep them in the urban area with this kind of a line with constant defence because Ilidza itself strategically speaking because, as you can see for yourself, was outside of Sarajevo and the central part of Bosnia, and their forces constantly tried to break through Ilidza --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, when you are answering my question, can you tell us that in this -- are you telling us that there was frequent fighting in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: There was fighting on a daily basis. There was fierce fighting, frequent fighting, high-intensity fighting, a lot of projectiles fired from the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, when you tell us that in the area of your brigade there was daily fighting, can you first tell us how far away were lines of demarcation from each other in this part of the area of responsibility of your brigade, when we are speaking about the lines of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Well, in this part and I can show also on the map, that sometimes we were only divided by a street or a couple of streets and sometimes the distance was 20 to 50 metres only, between our lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, bearing in mind that you said that you gathered information, in which way did you gather information while you were at this post where your duty was to gather, to collect information? How did you do this and how did you get to this information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Well, information was gathered in the information was passed on to us by the battalion commanders, chiefs for security, then through personal intelligence information speaking to the people across from the other side from Sarajevo who went -- who came through minefields and came over to our side because they were no longer able to stand torture and mistreatment in Sarajevo. And these people who crossed over from Sarajevo, they were a source of the most valuable information, those people who came and told us this information.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, in the period --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just have a look at the map, the original one. Yes, could -- Madam Usher, could you please assist.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, can you tell us whether you have personally have data which weapons BH Army soldiers used in the area of responsibility in your brigade -- of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Well, in the area of responsibility of the brigade, of my brigade where I was, the Muslims fired with all kinds of weapons known, classical weapons with the infantry weapons, rifles, semi-automatic machine-guns, machine-guns, anti-aircraft machine-guns, field guns, hand held rocket launchers. Rocket launchers like Zoljas, and even an Osa and even multiple rocket launchers: Howitzers, tanks, self-propelled guns.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, can you please speak slowly. And now that you have told us all this, are you telling us this on the basis of your personal knowledge about the weapons that the BH Army had at its disposal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: I am speaking from my personal knowledge because I suffered this fire, I was subjected to this fire from these weapons. Myself personally and the entire brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, when you've told us that Muslim -- that BH Army soldiers fired from tanks, can you tell us in which period and from which positions did they fire from tanks and I am talking about your personal experience, your personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Well, after I had returned from the hospital and after I had gone to Ilidza, a few days later, Ilidza was shelled. Tanks fired on Ilidza. Our observers reported this. They fired from the Sipad factory. It is a factory where furniture is produced and it is right next to the Jusuf Dzonlic Barracks at Stup.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, can you mark the area that you have said in which the BH Army acted in 1992 from September, can you mark this area on the map, the Jusuf Dzonlic Barracks and the furniture factory, can you mark these sites. Mr. DP17, take a felt tip and draw a circle and write the number "1" in the circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, I can't see very well now, but the witness has marked the area --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please stop. Don't mark anything on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: This is the standard furniture factory and this is the Jusuf Dzonlic Barracks here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, can you also mark the Jusuf Dzonlic Barracks with the number "2."

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the witness has marked the building of the Sipad company at Stup. He has marked this area, this site with number "1." He has used number "2" to mark the area where the Jusuf Dzonlic Barracks was located. And according to what the witness told us, tanks fired, BH Army tanks fired from there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness marks something on a clear question of you, there is no need to repeat anything for the transcript. That's mainly of importance if it is not marked when he just points at something. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, you have marked these two sites and you said that the tanks fired from there. Can you now tell us whether you personally knew whether in other areas of the zone of responsibility of your brigade there were positions from which the BH Army fired from tanks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Observers didn't see this but I personally saw it they fired from this hill, the Vitkovac Hill and from Brijesce Hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, I have to interrupt you then --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: I saw two tanks firing from there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Now that you have told us that, can you tell us during which period you observed this. We are talking about September 1992, August 1994, that is the period we are referring to. So when you say you personally saw this, can you tell us when you saw this, which positions you observed it from and at what time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: It was at the beginning of December 1992, that's when I personally saw them, at the beginning of December 1992. And when their offensive was launched in mid-June 1995, I saw those two tanks again --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, I have to interrupt you. We are not talking about 1995 now. So you have told us that it was in December 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: At the beginning of December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that at the beginning of December 1992 --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: I am talking about these tanks on Brijesce Brdo and Vitkovici Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, can you use number "3" to mark Vitkovici Brdo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: It's somewhere here. There are these houses here. And Brijesce Brdo is around here in this part, number 4. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. DP17. Mr. DP17, you mentioned the tanks of the BH Army. Can you tell us whether there were any tanks in your brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many there were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Well, these were T-55 tanks. There were three tanks. They often went to the technical and maintenance service because of wear and tear. Very often they were defective.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP17, you spoke about the weapons that the BH Army disposed of, that the BH Army had, and you told us that they also fired from field guns. Can you tell us and can you mark this on the map. Can you tell us which positions were positions from which BH Army members used field guns, if you have personal knowledge of this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: On Mojmilo, there was Santica Brdo which faces part of Nedzarici and Serbian Dobrinja. My personal knowledge relates to two field guns. One was by the long-distance power line. There was one field gun there. That will be number "5."

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, mark that with number "5" for the field gun --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: That was by the power line at the Mojmilo Brdo and the second one was in this area. I can't see the contour on this map, but it was about 50 metres away -- just a minute. I can perhaps mark it with greater precision. It was in this part, the second field gun was here. I will mark it with a number "6." And their task was to cover and fire on this part of Nedzarici and Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, you also spoke about --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: That's in this part. They had 150 -- 5 millimetre field guns on Igman because when they fired, this is a powerful weapon and you could hear the shell coming from the direction of Igman and they had 130 millimetre gun and 105 millimetre guns. These field guns were located according to our intelligence in Veliko Polje in Igman.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP17, you spoke about weapons and you mentioned multiple rocket launchers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you personally know for the period September 1992, August 1994, can you tell us whether they were used and when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Up until August 1994, well, they were used -- I know that at one point in time and I personally experienced this, I was at home, the children would go to school, my three daughters were to go to school and that's when a multiple rocket launcher was used and it fired at that area. I remember that I ran out to bring them back into the house as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, you haven't answered my question. I asked you which positions they fired from and when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: From Igman, that was towards the end of April and it was at the beginning of May. They were used from the Igman position. It is more easier -- it is easier to determine that position because when such shells -- when such rockets are fired from multiple rocket launcher, a terrible noise is made.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, could you please be brief. You haven't told me when they were used.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: End of April, beginning of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP17, you told us that the BH Army had mortars too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: They had mortars, they had 60-millimetre, 82-millimetre, and 81-millimetre mortars and 120-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you personally knew from which positions the mortars were fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Yes, from Sokolovici Kolonija, Hrasnica, Glava Gordinja [phoen], from the Mladjene neighbourhood which can be seen on this map I'll point it out. That is this neighbourhood here near the third phase, near Alipasino Polje --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP17, please -- could you please speak slowly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Should I repeat that?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mark the mortar positions on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Position 7, one of the positions; second position, Sokolovici Kolonija position number 8; here in the depth towards Mount Igman, position number 9; and from Glava Gordinja between Glava Gordinja from Hrasnica at the foot of Mount Igman, position number 10, there were mortars there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have not been precise enough. You said the witness mentioned mortars. Was that in the catalog of the weapons he gave or -- I don't see mortars there. I read all kinds of weapons known, classical weapons, the infantry weapons, rifles. I don't find the word "mortars" there. Of course, you referred to his testimony rather than ask him a new question. But I might have overlooked it that he said this at an earlier --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague will assist me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, 43.19 on my page in response to an answer from Ms. Pilipovic, but we have five pages -- we are five pages late, so that would be page 48.20, more or less. And Ms. Pilipovic asked whether there were any mortars and the witness said, as far as I can remember, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I was searching on the word "mortar" and I couldn't find any mortars back, so that is the reason why I am asking you. Because I wondered whether there was anything I might have missed or might not have been translated completely. When I search back on the word "mortar" I don't find it, but perhaps my computer is not doing what I want it to do. But please proceed. I just wondered whether I -- either the transcript or my ears missed something.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. DP17, slowly please, you marked the position of mortars in the direction of Sokolovic Kolonija, Hrasnica, Igman with number 10?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP17
utterances.text: Yes, and then there were others which were located by the restaurant Una, that is this part here. There was an office of T-A-M, Tam. I can still see it but although this map is recent, so that would be position number 11. They were located here in the Jusuf Dzonlic barracks too. They were in the Vranica company.
